title: Live validate scheduled-event event_load cutover
description: Prove the scheduled-event catalog path in the running Alpaca stack and retire or disable the CSV bridge only after runtime evidence matches or improves current behavior.
design: Run the catalog-backed event_load path through local checks, container config/status, and market-hours live validation. Capture before/after event_load freshness, coverage metadata, admission block behavior, unavailable reasons, dry_run_only reason if any, and broker/account status. Remove or explicitly disable CSV bridge wiring after parity is proven.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Runtime config/status uses the scheduled-event catalog path. 2. event_load reports fresh with expected coverage/source/policy metadata when catalog data is current. 3. Missing/stale/out-of-window catalog data reports explicit unavailable reasons. 4. EntryAdmission event_shock_earnings matches or improves previous CSV behavior. 5. Market-hours scan proves event_load is not the dry_run_only reason when data is current. 6. CSV bridge is removed or disabled after validation.

title: Add approved scheduled-event runtime loader
description: Add the read-only runtime loader that queries approved scheduled events and returns event_load-ready records plus coverage/freshness diagnostics.
design: The loader queries ApprovedScheduledEvent custom data by event_type, as_of_date, underlyings, and horizon. It returns approved events, source set, policy version, coverage min/max, freshness status, and unavailable reason. The router and admission callers receive normalized data from the loader; they do not query the catalog directly.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Loader reads approved events from ParquetDataCatalog. 2. Loader exposes event count, source set, policy version, coverage window, freshness status, and unavailable reason. 3. Missing/stale/out-of-window data is explicit. 4. No direct provider/CSV parsing is added to routing or admission. 5. Targeted validation covers fresh, missing, stale/out-of-window cases.

title: Write Alpha Vantage and manual earnings observations to catalog
description: Move earnings ingest from CSV-only output toward scheduled-event catalog writes. Alpha Vantage remains the first provider adapter and manual overrides become a source adapter with provenance.
design: Extend earnings-sync or its replacement path so provider rows produce raw evidence plus ScheduledEventObservation custom data. Add a simple manual override input path that writes observations with source=manual_override rather than editing approved outputs directly. CSV outputs may remain as bridge artifacts during this slice, but catalog observations must be the durable output.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Alpha Vantage ingest writes raw evidence and ScheduledEventObservation records. 2. Manual override observations can be written with provenance. 3. CSV bridge output, if still emitted, is explicitly secondary. 4. Ingest output includes enough metadata to support resolver freshness and source diagnostics. 5. Targeted validation proves observation catalog writes.
close_reason: Extended earnings-sync to retain Alpha Vantage raw evidence metadata, convert Alpha Vantage and manual override rows into ScheduledEventObservation records, and write observation CustomData batches to the configured scheduled-event ParquetDataCatalog while keeping CSV outputs as bridge artifacts. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins, cargo check -p nautilus-cli --features alpaca --bin nautilus, and a temp earnings-sync command run that wrote alpha_vantage and manual_override observation Parquet files.

title: Resolve and approve scheduled earnings events
description: Add the source-neutral resolver and approval policy that turns earnings observations into canonical decisions and strategy-safe approved events.
design: Implement deterministic resolver behavior over ScheduledEventObservation records: dedupe, source precedence, symbol and timing normalization, conflict/uncertain status, confidence, and resolver version. Implement approval policy that writes ApprovedScheduledEvent records with approved/block_only/rejected status, block window, policy version, and diagnostic reason. Unknown/conflicted timing remains conservative.
acceptance_criteria: 1. ScheduledEventDecision records are produced from observations. 2. ApprovedScheduledEvent records are produced from decisions. 3. Unknown timing, conflicts, weekend dates, and non-common symbols follow conservative policy. 4. block_only behavior exists for uncertain but risk-relevant events. 5. Targeted validation proves decision and approved-event catalog writes.

title: Wire Alpaca event_load and admission to scheduled-event loader
description: Cut Alpaca scanner/admission from direct CSV event ownership to the approved scheduled-event loader while preserving event_load and event_shock_earnings behavior.
design: Alpaca runtime config should point to the scheduled-event catalog and event policy. CandidateScanActor maps loader output into RegimeEvent inputs. EntryAdmission consumes the same approved event set for event_shock_earnings. Status and check-config report catalog path, event count, source set, policy version, coverage, freshness, unavailable reason, and whether event_load drives dry_run_only. CSV remains only as an explicit fallback/bridge during validation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. CandidateScanActor event_load uses loader output. 2. EntryAdmission event_shock_earnings uses the same approved event set. 3. Status/check-config expose loader diagnostics. 4. CSV feed config is disabled or explicitly bridge-only. 5. Targeted Alpaca checks pass.

title: Define scheduled-event custom data contracts and catalog smoke
description: Create the neutral scheduled-event domain contracts and prove they can round-trip through ParquetDataCatalog as Nautilus CustomData before wiring any Alpaca runtime behavior.
design: Add ScheduledEventObservation, ScheduledEventDecision, and ApprovedScheduledEvent as source-neutral scheduled-event custom data types. Keep them outside Alpaca-specific modules if the crate boundaries allow it; the Alpaca adapter may consume them, but should not own the model. Include the minimal catalog root/path handling needed for a local write/read proof. Do not connect runtime event_load or admission in this slice.

The types register and round-trip through ParquetDataCatalog. 3. A configurable catalog root uses NAUTILUS_SCHEDULED_EVENT_CATALOG with documented defaults. 4. No Alpaca runtime behavior changes in this slice. 5. Targeted format/build checks pass.

description: Refine the scheduled-event architecture documents after choosing the Parquet engine direction. Keep the target architecture intact while reducing duplication, removing stale CSV wording, and making current bridge wiring visibly temporary.

Active docs consistently name Parquet approved scheduled events as the target and CSV as migration-only. 3. Scanner/regime docs do not imply the router consumes external files, provider APIs, or raw signals directly. 4. Deploy examples that still reference CSV are marked as temporary bridge wiring until the Parquet reader is live. 5. git diff --check passes.

title: Implement Parquet scheduled-event engine for earnings event-load
description: Build the scheduled-event engine defined by docs/developer_guide/scheduled_event_engine.md and migrate Alpaca earnings event-load from the temporary CSV bridge to source-neutral scheduled-event custom data persisted through ParquetDataCatalog. Earnings is the first use case, but the implementation should support multiple source adapters and future event types without making Alpaca or Alpha Vantage the event model.
design: Implement source adapters that write raw evidence plus ScheduledEventObservation custom data through ParquetDataCatalog, starting with Alpha Vantage and a manual override source. Add resolver logic that emits ScheduledEventDecision custom data with source precedence, deduplication, symbol/timing normalization, conflicts, confidence, and policy versioning. Add approval policy that emits ApprovedScheduledEvent custom data, including block_only for uncertain but risk-relevant events. Add a read-only runtime loader that queries approved custom data by event_type, as_of_date, underlyings, and horizon, then returns events plus coverage/source/policy/freshness metadata. Wire Alpaca candidate scan and entry admission through the loader so RegimeEvent/EventLoadFeatures and event_shock_earnings use the same approved event set. Keep CSV support only as a temporary migration bridge, then remove it after live validation proves the catalog path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A configurable scheduled-event ParquetDataCatalog root is supported, defaulting to $XDG_STATE_HOME/nautilus_trader/scheduled_events/catalog or $HOME/.local/state/nautilus_trader/scheduled_events/catalog. 2. Alpha Vantage earnings ingest writes raw evidence plus ScheduledEventObservation, ScheduledEventDecision, and ApprovedScheduledEvent custom data following scheduled_event_engine.md. 3. Manual overrides are modeled as a source adapter with provenance, not direct edits to approved output. 4. Resolver and approval policy handle source conflicts, unknown timing, weekend/non-common symbols, block_only behavior, and policy versioning conservatively. 5. Alpaca event_load and EntryAdmission read approved events through the runtime loader, not direct CSV parsing. 6. Operator status/check-config report catalog path, event count, source set, policy version, coverage window, freshness, and unavailable reason. 7. Current CSV feed support is removed or clearly disabled after ParquetDataCatalog live validation passes. 8. Live validation proves event_load freshness and admission blocks match or improve current behavior.

title: Document Parquet scheduled-event engine architecture
description: Refine the earnings/event-load workstream into the durable architecture: earnings is the first scheduled-event use case, not an Alpaca-owned scanner feature. The target is a source-neutral scheduled-event engine with source adapters, raw evidence retention, Parquet observation/decision/approved datasets, resolver/approval policy, and a read-only runtime loader that supplies RegimeEvent/EventLoadFeatures plus entry-admission blocks. Alpha Vantage and Alpaca may remain the first proof path, but raw vendor data and generated CSV feeds must not be the long-term runtime contract.
design: Target model: source adapters such as Alpha Vantage fetch provider data and retain raw evidence, then write normalized ScheduledEventObservation Parquet. A resolver merges observations into canonical ScheduledEventDecision Parquet with source precedence, deduplication, symbol normalization, timing normalization, conflict detection, and confidence. Approval policy writes ApprovedScheduledEvent Parquet as the only strategy-safe dataset. Default catalog root should be NAUTILUS_SCHEDULED_EVENT_CATALOG, falling back to $XDG_STATE_HOME/nautilus_trader/scheduled_events or $HOME/.local/state/nautilus_trader/scheduled_events. Postgres may hold small ingest manifests/watermarks, but event facts live in Parquet. Runtime components use a read-only scheduled-event loader to query approved Parquet by event_type/as_of_date/underlyings/horizon and convert approved events into source-neutral RegimeEvent inputs for crates/trading/src/options/regime.rs. EntryAdmission consumes the same approved event set for deterministic event_shock_earnings blocks. Current earnings_events.csv and earnings_events_approved.csv wiring is migration support only; it should be removed after the Parquet reader validates live. Do not add fixed-expiry live flags, auto/fixed scanner modes, direct provider calls from routing, raw CSV parsing in decision code, or a separate earnings scanner.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Active architecture docs describe earnings as the first scheduled-event use case and define a source-neutral scheduled-event engine, not an Alpaca-owned feed or scanner. 2. Docs specify Parquet as the durable storage for normalized observations, resolver decisions, and approved scheduled events, with raw provider payloads retained only as audit evidence. 3. Docs define the default catalog root, dataset layout, core observation/decision/approved schemas, resolver responsibility, approval policy responsibility, and read-only runtime loader contract. 4. Docs explain multi-source adapters, manual overrides as a source adapter, conflict handling, unknown timing behavior, and conservative block_only behavior. 5. Regime/scanner docs make the router consume normalized event-load inputs from the loader, not raw CSV, provider APIs, or the catalog directly. 6. Existing CSV earnings feed paths are documented only as current migration wiring, not the target runtime contract. 7. The docs explicitly reject duplicate earnings scanner loops, direct Alpaca/vendor calls from routing, fixed-expiry live control flags, and placeholder neutral regime labels. 8. The bead cross-references nt-x0o market-hours validation so architecture closure and live proof stay connected.
close_reason: Documented the Parquet scheduled-event engine architecture in docs/developer_guide/scheduled_event_engine.md, linked it from developer guide index, updated regime/scanner/production docs, aligned AGENTS.md active guidance, and created nt-x0o.2 for implementation migration from CSV bridge to approved Parquet runtime loader.

title: Market-hours live validation for profile-owned Alpaca options runtime
description: Run a focused market-hours validation pass for the profile-owned Alpaca options runtime after the architecture cleanup. The goal is to prove the fresh selected-candidate path and, when intentionally enabled, a bounded paper submit/cancel smoke through the Nautilus strategy path. Do not add fixed-expiry live flags, auto/fixed modes, or family-list switches.
design: Use shipped CLIs/container commands and the existing Docker/systemd runtime. Prefer observation first: check config, account, orders, positions, universe coverage, profile-tagged scans, and entry decisions. Only enable paper submission with explicit safety gates such as one-shot iteration, quantity 1, paper endpoints, and cancel-after-accept. If no selected candidate appears, record that honestly as scan/runtime proof rather than broker-submission proof. No code changes or automated tests unless validation exposes a real defect.
acceptance_criteria: Market-hours run records container/service health and broker account status; check-config reports strategy_profiles and universe_intents; status shows profile-tagged universe/scanner state; a fresh selected-candidate decision includes profile identity when market data produces one; any intentional paper order smoke cancels accepted orders and ends with open orders 0 and no unintended positions; close reason includes exact commands and evidence, including whether broker submission was or was not proven.

title: Add option universe rollover and stale-series lifecycle
description: The live service runs continuously, so selected option series must roll forward without manual .env edits or container restarts. Add a scanner/universe lifecycle that re-resolves on trade-date rollover or when selected series drift outside their DTE windows, then unsubscribes stale series through Nautilus APIs.
design: Use Nautilus timers/lifecycle hooks in the actor path. Do not add a standalone rollover daemon.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Universe resolver refreshes on trade-date rollover and stale-DTE detection.
2. Stale series are unsubscribed with Nautilus unsubscribe_option_chain.
3. Newly selected series are requested/subscribed without restarting the node.
4. Active strategy entries and active-risk quote subscriptions are not disrupted by universe rollover.
5. Operator evidence records rollover decisions, selected replacements, and skipped underlyings.
close_reason: Added source-neutral DTE lifecycle helpers and actor-owned universe refresh lifecycle. Dynamic scanner universe now re-requests instruments on trade-date rollover or stale selected-series DTE, reconciles profile/underlying selections, subscribes replacements, unsubscribes stale scanner series with unsubscribe_option_chain when unused, and emits option_universe_refresh/option_universe_rollover/subscription evidence. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-trading -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo check -p nautilus-trading, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bin alpaca-options-node, and git diff --check.

title: Remove fixed option expiry from live alpaca-options-node
description: Remove the live engine dependency on ALPACA_OPTION_CHAIN_EXPIRY, positional EXPIRY, and live settlement flags. alpaca-options-node should wire runtime config, data client, execution client, scanner actor, account strategy, persistence, and lifecycle only. Fixed-expiry filters may remain in explicit diagnostic/backtest commands.
design: This is a rip-out, not an auto|fixed mode flag. The live node should not contain a compatibility lane for fixed-expiry runtime selection.
acceptance_criteria:
1. alpaca-options-node no longer requires positional EXPIRY or ALPACA_OPTION_CHAIN_EXPIRY to start.
2. alpaca-options-node no longer builds live OptionSeriesIds in the runner/node layer.
3. Live compose/.env/operator guidance no longer exposes fixed-expiry or settlement controls for the engine path.
4. Diagnostic/backtest commands that intentionally filter by expiry remain explicit and documented as non-live controls.
5. --check-config reports strategy profile universe intent and does not imply a fixed live series list.
close_reason: Removed fixed-expiry live controls from alpaca-options-node and compose, left explicit expiry controls scoped to compare/diagnostics, and updated live runner docs. --check-config now reports strategy-derived universe_intents instead of a live series list. title: Refactor option-chain scanner to resolve strategy universe dynamically
description: Refactor OptionChainCandidateScanActor so the live path consumes strategy-profile universe intent instead of a static Vec<OptionSeriesId> from alpaca-options-node. The actor should request instruments through Nautilus data requests, resolve selected series through the source-neutral universe model, subscribe/unsubscribe with subscribe_option_chain, and scan slices only for the profiles that selected that series.
design: Do not subscribe to every expiry in the DTE window. Until multi-expiry aggregation exists, choose a deterministic target series per profile/underlying to avoid acting on whichever slice publishes first.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Live scanner config accepts strategy-derived universe intent rather than fixed live series from env.
2. Actor requests option instruments by underlying/DTE window/required side through Nautilus request_instruments params.
3. Actor handles response-level instrument results, including zero-contract responses.
4. Actor maintains profile+underlying -> selected series and series -> profile mappings.
5. OptionChainSlice scans are restricted to strategy profiles that selected the slice series.
6. Explicit static series remains limited to catalog/backtest/diagnostic use, not live env control.
7. The scanner emits source-neutral universe resolution evidence.
close_reason: Implemented strategy-derived live universe resolution in OptionChainCandidateScanActor, removed live fixed-series construction from alpaca-options-node, scoped scan jobs to profiles selected by the neutral resolver, and emitted option_universe_resolution diagnostics. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bin alpaca-options-node, and git diff --check.

title: Expose InstrumentsResponse-level hooks to DataActor
description: DataActor currently handles InstrumentsResponse by iterating each instrument into on_instrument. Empty instrument responses disappear, which caused zero-contract universe requests to have no actor-visible outcome. Add a source-neutral response-level hook so universe resolution can observe correlation ids, request params, and empty responses while preserving existing on_instrument behavior by default.
design: Prefer on_instruments_response(&InstrumentsResponse) or equivalent. The callback should keep Nautilus response semantics intact and avoid adapter-specific special cases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. DataActor exposes an overridable InstrumentsResponse-level callback with response metadata and data length.
2. Default behavior preserves existing behavior by iterating instruments through on_instrument.
3. Actors can override the response-level hook to handle empty responses without duplicating common wiring.
4. The hook lives in common/data actor code and contains no Alpaca-specific concepts.
5. Existing request_instruments routing still works for current actors.
close_reason: Added DataActor::on_instruments_response(&InstrumentsResponse) in crates/common/src/actor/data_actor.rs. The default implementation preserves existing per-instrument dispatch through on_instrument, while handle_instruments_response now invokes the response-level hook for both populated and empty responses. No adapter-specific concepts added. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-common; cargo check -p nautilus-common; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; diff review confirmed the hook-only common-code change.

title: Introduce source-neutral option universe intent and resolution model
description: Create source-neutral option-universe domain types outside crates/adapters/alpaca. The model should represent strategy intent and resolution outcomes: profile id, underlying, strategy family, required option sides, DTE window, target-DTE/selection policy, selected OptionSeriesId metadata, and structured skip reasons. It must be reusable by live, replay, and backtest paths.
design: Likely home is a source-neutral options module under trading/model layers, not nautilus_alpaca. Keep provider inputs generic enough to adapt Alpaca contracts/instruments without baking in Alpaca response shapes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Universe intent/resolution types live outside crates/adapters/alpaca and import no Alpaca adapter types.
2. Model represents required side semantics for put credit, call credit, iron condor, debit, and naked option profiles.
3. Resolution supports deterministic selection of a small target set, initially one expiry per profile/underlying, favoring the configured DTE window midpoint.
4. Resolution produces structured selected/skipped outcomes with reasons such as no_contracts_in_window, missing_required_side, outside_dte_window, and provider_error.
5. The model can be consumed by live scanner actors and read-only backtest/replay tooling.
close_reason: Added source-neutral option universe intent/resolution model in crates/trading/src/options/universe.rs and exported it from crates/trading/src/options/mod.rs. The model covers profile intent, strategy-family side requirements, DTE windows, target/midpoint selection policy, selected OptionSeriesId coverage, and structured skip reasons including no_contracts_in_window, outside_dte_window, missing_required_side, and provider_error. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-trading; cargo check -p nautilus-trading; git diff --check for tracked edits; trailing-whitespace scan; targeted Alpaca-import and fixed-mode phrase searches.

title: Document option universe ownership boundary
description: Capture the architecture decision before implementation so future work does not drift back into env-driven fixed-expiry control. The decision must define ownership across source-neutral options models, Nautilus DataEngine/OptionChainManager, Alpaca data providers, scanner actors, account strategy, backtest/replay, and operator diagnostics.
design: Use repo architecture style and active docs. Do not preserve stale compatibility language as live guidance.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ADR or architecture note explains why live fixed-expiry flags are rejected.
2. Documented boundary says strategy profiles own universe intent, neutral resolver owns selection semantics, adapters provide market-specific instruments/contracts, and Nautilus owns concrete subscriptions.
3. Document identifies the high-load constraint: do not subscribe to every expiry in a DTE window until candidate aggregation supports complete multi-expiry cycles.
4. Document distinguishes live strategy-driven resolution from explicit fixed-expiry diagnostic/backtest filters.
close_reason: Documented source-neutral option universe ownership boundary in docs/developer_guide/option_universe_ownership.md; linked it from the developer guide index and docs/concepts/options.md; validated with git diff --check for tracked edits, trailing-whitespace scan for edited docs, link target checks, and targeted fixed-mode phrase search.

title: Make live option universe Nautilus-native
description:

design:

- Provide generic spread id parse/build helpers equivalent to the existing Python generic_spread_id_to_list()/new_generic_spread_id() syntax: positive ratios as `(ratio)SYMBOL`, negative ratios as `((ratio))SYMBOL`, joined by `___`.

title: Fix backtester reduce-only spread closes using neutral spread package semantics
description:
Synthetic Nautilus backtests prove aggregate OptionSpread quotes and signed spread open/close fills work: a put-credit spread aggregated to negative quotes, Buy OptionSpread filled at the negative ask, and a non-reduce-only Sell OptionSpread flattened generated leg positions. However, reduce_only Sell OptionSpread close is rejected with would-have-increased-position because the backtester validates reduce-only against a parent spread instrument position while spread accounting intentionally stores economic positions on generated legs.

The fix should not create parent spread positions, because ExecutionEngine treats combo/spread fills as order-management events and leg fills as the economic position source. Instead, once nt-ups.8 promotes generic spread leg semantics to neutral model helpers, the backtester should evaluate reduce-only for spread orders against the leg-position package implied by the spread ratios.
design:
Backtester target behavior:

- Keep existing single-instrument reduce-only behavior unchanged.
- For spread instruments, resolve signed spread legs from neutral model helpers, not Alpaca code.
- Derive each child leg close side from parent spread side plus signed ratio.
- Look up open leg positions by leg instrument, strategy, and account.
- Require every spread leg to reduce an existing opposite-side leg position; missing, same-side, closed, or insufficient leg packages must reject/cancel as reduce-only.
- Compute max_closeable_spread_qty as min(open_leg_qty / abs(ratio)) across all legs, then cap oversized reduce-only parent spread fills to that package quantity, matching the existing single-instrument reduce-only cap behavior.
- Generate synthetic leg fills only for the actual applied parent spread fill quantity after reduce-only capping.
- Make spread fills atomic from an accounting perspective: if leg prices/quotes are unavailable and leg fills cannot be generated, the parent spread fill must not silently leave no economic position evidence.
- Keep direct spread QuoteTick support honest: it can only be used for order matching when leg quotes/prices are also available for accounting, or it must reject with explicit evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. This work consumes neutral spread leg helpers from nt-ups.8 and does not import or duplicate Alpaca-owned generic spread parsing.
2. Submission-time reduce-only validation for OptionSpread/FuturesSpread orders recognizes the existing leg-position package implied by the spread ratios.
3. Fill-time reduce-only cancellation/clamping for market and limit spread orders uses max_closeable_spread_qty across legs.
4. Synthetic spread leg fills are generated from the actual applied parent fill quantity after reduce-only capping.
5. A spread parent fill cannot succeed while leg fill generation/accounting silently fails due missing leg quotes or instruments.
6. A synthetic aggregate-spread proof can Buy a credit/debit vertical OptionSpread and then Sell reduce_only to flatten generated leg positions.
7. Four-leg iron-condor reduce-only behavior is covered or explicitly documented as unsupported before implementation closes.
8. Ordinary single-instrument reduce-only behavior remains unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented backtester reduce-only spread close handling against generated leg positions. Spread orders now compute closeable package quantity from signed spread legs and indexed leg positions, apply the same reduce-only cap to parent fills, require leg quote/instrument availability before parent fills, and generate synthetic leg fills from the actual applied parent fills. title: Rework Alpaca spreads onto Nautilus-native spread support
description: Replace remaining fork-local spread pricing/planning paths with Nautilus-native spread instruments, spread quote aggregation, and strategy/order APIs. Account for upstream spread quote controls such as disable_vega_pricing and vega_pricing_timeout_seconds, preserve Alpaca multi-leg order behavior, and keep scanner/strategy evidence source-neutral.
design:
Problem

The current Alpaca options path uses SelectedOptionsEntry/SpreadCandidate as too many things at once: scanner output, quote snapshot, premium source, order-shape source, and strategy-state evidence. Under heavy load this is the design flaw. A candidate premium can be stale by the time admission and execution run, and there is no single orderable spread identity tying together the live quote, limit price, state, and broker payload.

Ideal target model

Make the orderable domain object a Nautilus OptionSpread. Candidate selection should pick legs and explain why; it should not be the execution pricing model.

Introduce a small spread planning layer, preferably source-neutral if the first slice shows it is not Alpaca-specific:

- OptionSpreadPlan, or similarly named durable type, built from SelectedOptionsEntry plus venue/cache metadata.
- Output includes InstrumentAny::OptionSpread, spread InstrumentId, leg InstrumentIds, signed ratios, strategy family, quantity, entry side, premium kind, and scanner evidence.
- The spread InstrumentId symbol must use the existing Nautilus generic spread syntax parsed by DataEngine: positive legs as `(ratio)SYMBOL`, negative legs as `((ratio))SYMBOL`, joined by `___`, under the Alpaca venue.
- Define ratios from the desired entry package: bought/long legs are positive, sold/short legs are negative. Open entries can then be represented as buying the planned spread; credit packages naturally have negative prices, which Nautilus Price and spread aggregation support.
- Examples: a put credit entry is `(1)LONG_PUT___((1))SHORT_PUT.ALPACA`; a call debit entry is `(1)LONG_CALL___((1))SHORT_CALL.ALPACA`; an iron condor extends the same pattern to four legs.

Market data model

Register the OptionSpread in the Nautilus cache before subscribing or ordering. Subscribe to the spread instrument with params including `aggregate_spread_quotes=true`; DataEngine will parse the spread legs from the spread symbol, subscribe leg quotes, run SpreadQuoteAggregator, insert the synthetic QuoteTick into cache, and publish the spread quote topic.

For Alpaca migration, set `disable_vega_pricing=true` initially unless we wire a fresh greeks provider with a clear freshness SLO. Use component bid/ask quote pricing as the default because it is explicit and operationally safe. When greeks freshness is proven, enable vega pricing per family/config and record `vega_pricing_enabled`, `vega_pricing_temporarily_disabled`, and greeks timestamps in evidence.

Entry pricing and admission

Use the cached spread QuoteTick as the entry limit source. Candidate premium remains scanner evidence only. Admission should block when the spread quote is missing, stale, crossed/invalid, or deviates from the scanner premium beyond a configured tolerance. Persist the pricing source and comparison details so dry-run and post-trade analysis can explain each decision.

Execution model

The clean end state is a single Nautilus Limit order on the OptionSpread instrument, with the signed net spread limit as the order price. AlpacaExecutionClient should support InstrumentAny::OptionSpread in submit_order by expanding the cached spread instrument legs into an Alpaca mleg payload:

- Parse legs with the same generic spread leg syntax DataEngine uses.
- Derive Alpaca leg side and position_intent from order side, signed ratio, and reduce_only.
- Use the order quantity as strategy quantity and abs(ratio) as each leg ratio_qty.
- Use the order price as Alpaca's signed net limit price, preserving negative credit prices.
- Emit parent order lifecycle against the spread order and store broker parent/leg IDs as evidence.

The existing SubmitOrderList path is a useful staged bridge for current leg-based submission and close handling, but it should not be the destination. If a first implementation needs it, carry an explicit net limit in SubmitOrderList params rather than re-deriving the broker limit from stale per-leg candidate prices, and treat that as a temporary migration step.

State and evidence

Strategy state should move toward spread identity first: spread_instrument_id, spread_raw_symbol, leg symbols/ids/ratios, entry order id, entry quote bid/ask/ts, signed entry limit, scanner premium, quote-vs-scanner delta, pricing_source, vega mode, and greeks freshness. Existing short_symbol/long_symbol fields can remain during migration, but new logic should key active spread exposure by spread_instrument_id plus order id.

Candidate ledger/performance evidence should distinguish scanner evidence from execution pricing. Useful labels: `scanner_snapshot`, `nautilus_spread_quote`, `leg_quote_fallback`, and `broker_fill`. Do not make ClickHouse or Parquet the source of truth for broker evidence; keep operational state slim in Postgres/state files and use market-data stores for quote history.

Migration phases

Phase 0: inventory and tests around the existing candidate/order/state paths. Confirm all spread families and close flows that depend on SelectedOptionsEntry fields.

Phase 1: add OptionSpreadPlan and deterministic spread instrument creation. Register/cache spread instruments and subscribe aggregate spread quotes for dry-run candidates, no behavior change.

Phase 2: add dry-run comparison and admission evidence. Compare old candidate premium against cached spread QuoteTick for top candidates and block on missing/stale/deviating spread quotes. Start with vertical put_credit/call_credit before debit and iron_condor.

Phase 3: implement Alpaca OptionSpread submit expansion in the execution client and prove payload generation without broker submit. Add support for negative signed spread prices and ratio-derived leg intents.

Phase 4: switch one vertical family to spread-order dry-run, then paper submit only with explicit approval. Keep close management on existing leg logic until spread close/reconciliation is proven.

Phase 5: migrate close management, state/performance reads, debit spreads, and iron condors onto spread identity. Retire stale candidate-premium execution paths after live proof.

Risks and decisions

Main risks are spread instrument identity drift, stale or missing leg quotes, incorrect sign/ratio mapping into Alpaca MLeg, and reconciliation assumptions that currently expect one Nautilus order per leg. The design deliberately handles identity and pricing first, then broker expansion and reconciliation, instead of hiding the problem inside order-builder math.
acceptance_criteria:

2. Add a deterministic Nautilus OptionSpread plan/mapper for vertical credit/debit spreads first, including generic spread symbol syntax, leg ratios, entry side, and evidence fields.
3. Register/cache the spread instrument and subscribe its QuoteTick through DataEngine aggregate_spread_quotes with explicit vega-pricing policy.
4. Prove dry-run comparison between old candidate premium and live Nautilus spread quote, with stale/missing/deviation admission blocks.
5. Implement the ideal execution path as a single OptionSpread limit order expanded by AlpacaExecutionClient to MLeg; keep existing SubmitOrderList leg path only as a staged bridge until close/reconciliation migration is complete.
6. Validate with targeted Alpaca compile checks and an operator dry-run proof; do not submit paper orders unless explicitly approved.
